The most important conclusions of the paper are that conflict areas are not designed correctly, and the light intensity distribution curve for classical street lighting luminaire can change along the life of the equipment, which not only reduces the efficiency of the equipment, but actually it can even generate high light pollution.

articleTitle: Techniques and Indices for Preventive Maintenance optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The authors present a few techniques and the corresponding indices for preventive maintenance optimization (PMO). Following a comprehensive presentation of maintenance categories as well as their importance for industrial systems operation, the focus is oriented to the specific indices like average, median and maximum preventive maintenance duration. Techniques related to PMO are based on minimum out-of-service duration, reliability and average time to repair, optimum preventive maintenance frequency, economical benefits and preventive and corrective maintenance coordination. Finally, two Markov chain models for PMO are detailed. The models include both maintenance types: corrective and preventive.

articleTitle: Economic Assessment of Grid-Connected Residential Rooftop Photovoltaics with Battery Energy Storage System under Various Electricity Tariffs: A Case Study in Romania
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Solar energy has the highest potential among renewable energy sources to gradually replace fossil fuels in electricity generation, paving the road for a cleaner and sustainable energy future. Over the last few years, it has been noticed an increased deployment of grid-connected residential rooftop photovoltaic systems, especially due to their significant cost reduction. A valuable solution for solving the problem of temporal mismatch between the electricity generated by the photovoltaic system and electricity demand is the energy storage system. This paper aims to investigate the feasibility of gridconnected residential rooftop photovoltaics combined with battery energy storage system for a household in Romania taking into account different electricity tariffs. The results pointed out how the system's profitability is affected by the time of use electricity tariffs and the flat tariffs applied on Romanian residential customers that do not take into consideration the time of use.

articleTitle: Transient Power Quality Mitigation by Synchronized Capacitor Banks Switching
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The quality of the transient electricity is disturbed by the switching of the capacitor banks steps, thus affecting the equipment of the related electrical installation. The transitional regime may be defined as the variable mode of transition from an initial state of operation (a permanent regime) to another permanent regime. The transitional regime is generally a short-term one due to the short time constants of the electrical grids, but which may affect the security of electrical installations or the stability of their operation. Transitional phenomena resulting from the switching of capacitor banks are becoming more and more important, as the number of capacitor banks in the supply systems increases. This is because the most common operation is the capacitor banks switching, which can occur several times a day depending on the need of the reactive power/energy to stabilize voltage and maintain power factor in admissible limits. This paper analyzes, using EMTP software, the impact of capacitor transients for different scenarios and with different methods of mitigating the quality of electricity.

articleTitle: Design of Wireless Power Transfer Circuit for Stable Voltage Output
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: As a technology which can enhance charging safety and flexibility, wireless power transfer (WPT) was applied in some high-tech equipment, especially in aquatic drones, considering its complex charging environment. In order to improve the stability of wireless power transfer system voltage output while the relative position of two coils changing, a WPT circuit which can supply stable 12 V output voltage and current various with the distance changing between transmitting coil (Tx) and receiving coil (Rx) in a range from 5 mm to 30 mm is designed. To get the maximum transmission efficiency, the system is supposed to keep working at resonant frequency which is realized by frequency control chips for inverter in first side and rectifier in second side respectively. The detailed study of battery charging current versus coil distance is analyzed by simulation and experiment. In addition, the parameters of different circuit components such like capacity and inductance are fixed to obtain the resonance, which is determined by calculation and simulation. Meanwhile, the shape of coils is considered as well because it has clear affection on mutual inductance.

articleTitle: Benchmarking General-Purpose Neural Networks for Real-Time Pedestrian Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents the main steps and results on automotive applications aiming to detect pedestrians by means of object detection and recognition neural networks. The used training and testing datasets take into account the influence of different factors, such as environmental conditions and video-image acquisition characteristics, using a custom training and testing dataset, and critically evaluate the performance and capabilities of general-purpose neural networks in detecting pedestrians from usual images provided by a video camera.Following this goal, an analysis points out what differences occur in the final classification output of these neuronal networks using the same dataset for training while testing on real-life scenarios. In the end a general-purpose neural network which provides the best results in pedestrian detection (providing 2D bounding boxes) is proposed and its performances are discussed.

articleTitle: Study of Coils Impact For a Boost Converter Used in the Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper describes an analyse of different coil types and their behaviour in the boost convertor functionality during the several power output test. The presented study was used as a reference point for the integrated circuit (IC), ISL “78227”, circuit that has been used in the series production for automotive industry projects, especially as a boost converter driver. The purpose of the test was to determine if the integrated circuit is capable to drive and synchronize in between the phases for fuel injectors supply applications. The DC-DC boost converter was designed to rise up the voltage from 9V up to 50V and 55V, for different load conditions. During the test, a wide range of input voltages were taken into consideration, from 9V to 32V as case studies, and a wide range of power outputs. The work contains also a study of the synchronous functionality and phase balance in between two phases. However, the text of this paper is a continuation of the already published paper “Simulation of a Boost Converter for the Automotive Industry”.

articleTitle: Telerehabilitation Solution for Hand Therapy
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper proposes a telerehabilitation solution for hand Therapy. The proposed solution has two main components: the recovery part itself and the device for recording physiological parameters. We chose to record the heart rate and the EMG signal. To monitor heart rate during recovery exercises, we used a photoplethysmogram (PPG) sensor that picks up the earlobe signal. EMG module connected directly to the electrodes placed on the muscle whose activity is to be monitored for recording the EMG signal. To perform the recovery exercises, we made a game in Unity3D with several levels and degrees of complexity. After completing each level, the patient obtains a score depending on the correctness with which he performed the exercise. Before starting the recovery program, each patient was monitored with a Holter system for 24 hours, and an analysis of heart rate variation was performed. These results are considered a reference for analyzing the rhythm variability performed during the recovery program.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the measurement uncertainty in calibration of bell standard installation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)

authors.preferredName: Lecturer dr. eng. Gabriel Constantin Sârbu

abstract: The paper refers to evaluation of the measurement uncertainty in calibration of bell standard installation used for metrological verification of gas flow meters and gas meters. The evaluation and calculation of the measurement uncertainty is necessary because its knowledge is necessary to make good quality measurements and to understand and use the results of the measurements performed. The evaluation of the measurement uncertainty, as part of the calibration, is very important in demonstrating the capability of the calibration laboratories and which must be reported on the certificate. Is important firstly to identify the sources of uncertainty in the measurement, then we must estimate the contribution of the uncertainty from each source, finally the individual uncertainties are combined. The calibration of the bell installations used for the verification of the gas meters is performed by the direct comparison method using a metal volume measure of special construction, secondary standard.

articleTitle: A Battery Screening System for Second Life LiFePO₄ Batteries
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Once the first generation of Li-ion batteries that power electric vehicles will reach the End of Life, car manufacturers and local governments will face a real problem. The growing number of retired batteries, do not meet the automotive safety standards any more but still have around 80% of their initial capacity which makes them ideal for other applications. For their new job, they have to be properly evaluated so cells with similar characteristics are used in the same battery packs. This paper presents a method and a system that can very fast and accurately determine cells with similar characteristics. The system is used to screen LiFePO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (LFP), batteries on-site and sort cells based on their DC resistance. After this stage, they are tagged and evaluated through a common screening method.

articleTitle: Computer Modeling the Effect of Weak Electromagnetic Field on Charged Particles by Unity Engine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The problem of computer modeling and visualization of weak electromagnetic fields is important for research activity, education, biology, medicine and industry. Visualization helps better understanding and clarifying the physical and mathematical models that are used. In medicine low frequency magnetic fields are traditionally used in magnetotherapy, and at the moment computer modeling and visualization give the only practical approach to the studying the influence of magnetic fields on a living organism. In this work we designed and implemented an effective and adequate computer tool both for modeling a magnetic field distribution and the action of the field on charged particles. The tool is designed in the program environment Unity, which allows the combining calculations and visualization, considerable reducing run-time and the development of a flexible application that may be easily used by both practicians and researchers. The results of experiments are given.

articleTitle: Spatial Light Source Simulations For Near Field Reflections
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Linear lamps (fluorescent or LED) represent a suitable option for specific applications. For near field simulations, such as coves or luminaires, the usual mathematical representation is not sufficient. A photometric file (extension.IES or.LDT) is only valid for normal interior lighting, not for near field, and the traditional theory doesn't have any solving approach. The present paper proposes a method to solve these limitations, and a numerical model is developed and presented. The validation method is based on experimental results, for a test problem.

articleTitle: SAR Determination for Indoor, Far Field Exposure
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (field recently extended with bio-electromagnetic compatibility) is a never-ending challenge for any type of radio-frequency non-ionizing radiation. Human behavior in this ubiquitous field is anytime a topic of constant interest. Evaluation of short or long term impact of electromagnetic non-ionizing radiation on humans should be priority. We here share a case study focused on the estimation of specific absorption rate (SAR). The electromagnetic source has been considered as far-field communication system, while the 3D human model has been previously presented and tested by the authors. The evaluation of human exposure is performed by determining the SAR values on the surface of the 3D human body model placed inside an office room, in various exposure scenarios. The SAR values have been determined by simulations using a specialized software program, SIMULIA CST Suite Studio, the Microwave Module of the software. The obtained SAR values have been compared with the limits imposed by standards in force.

articleTitle: Detailed Modelling and Control of a Multiterminal High Voltage DC Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to modelling multiterminal high voltage DC networks using detailed equivalent schemes. Next, a thorough view is given to converter controller design, focusing on modulus optimum criterion for parameter tuning. Finally, the model and controller are validated using Matlab/Simulink.

Author Keywords: multiterminal high voltage direct current transmission

articleTitle: Simulation of a Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Minibus under Simcenter Amesim
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: New solutions that help reducing CO2 emissions and energy consumption need to be developed. Fuel cell is a promising solution but challenges remain significant in order to deploy it widely. This paper presents a hybrid electric bus control strategy that involve a Fuel Cell and a Battery as electric energy sources. The fuel cell provides the energy while the batteries are providing peak power to the vehicle. Simcenter Amesim platform is used to simulate the complete system for WLTC driving cycles. Also a comparative analysis between the performances of fuel cell hybrid and a pure battery electric minibus is made.

articleTitle: Using Kalman Filters for Increasing Accuracy of Distance Measurement Using a Single Camera
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: There are numerous situations in traffic where it is necessary to determine the distance to an object in front of a moving vehicle in order to warn the driver or, moreover, to automatically operate the car's safety system to avoid a collision. This paper proposes a method to improve the accuracy of distance measurement up to a fixed obstacle using only a video camera and speed information from the moving vehicle, through Kalman filtering (KF) procedures. The efficiency of the application of KF for the determination of the distance is proved by the decrease by more than one order of magnitude of the measurement error, being able to reach values below 1% under certain conditions presented in the paper. Because the KF algorithm is iterative and proved to be effective working on images acquired with a normal resolution camera, it does not require significant computing resources, so it can be run on modest microcontroller devices.

articleTitle: Video distance measurement based on focus
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In monovision field- distance determination with a single camera or video- the methods for determining distances are varied and we can divide them as follows: a) based on focusfixing the lens in the position corresponding to the maximum sharpness of the acquired image (DFF- depth-from focusing); b) based on the blur / defocus of the lenses - (DFD - depth-from defocusing); c) combined methods. The DFF method scans the “scene” by taking sequences of images with various lens settings and tries to find the best focus. This paper presents a method of measuring distances based on focus. It is used a web video camera. To achieve the autofocus, the camera lens moves to a position where the clearest image is obtained. The maximum clarity is measured from the histograms of the images on which a filter with the role of highlighting the edges was initially applied. Knowing the focal length of the lens, the distances can be found from the lens equation (1). Theoretically, for each position of the lens, in which the maximum clarity is reached, it corresponds a measured distance between the object and the camera. Because the camera used has only 16 positions of the lens, each position corresponds to a range of distances, this range being of the order of centimeters. Measurement accuracy can be improved by applying a linear and parabolic interpolation process. In this way the errors reach the order of millimeters. The distance measuring device in the present paper consists of a fixed video camera, a PC with the role of information processing and an object moving in front of the camera on its optical axis. Both the camera and the object are arranged on a graduated ruler support on which the camera is calibrated.

articleTitle: Wearable Device for Measurement of Exposure to Artificial Lighting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Studies show that a large number of people in the EU have disorders caused by artificial light or conditions that can be aggravated by light. Therefore, this research proposes the creation of a portable device (EXPILART device or EDEV) that can be used to measure exposure to artificial lighting and can communicate wireless with a cloud app. This paper presents an initial prototype of EDEV which is based on high performance system on a chip including a microcontroller and wireless module and light and other sensors. The proposed methodology reduces the complexity of EDEV, while allowing precise results to be obtained. EDEV will have a high level of integration and high autonomy by using miniaturized and low power components.

articleTitle: Design of Fractional Order Controllers for Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents aspects of robust control for a Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind turbine. The use of a fractional order proportional-integral (FOPI) controller is proposed, since ensures superior performances in comparison with the conventional proportional-integral (PI) controller, in presence of external disturbances, measurement noises and generator parameters variations. For a vector control structure of DFIG, a FOPI controller is designed and the results of simulation conducted in Matlab/Simulink are presented and compared to a conventional PI controller.

articleTitle: Research on the Realization of a Nitinol Clutch Type Thermocouple
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nowadays the use of smart materials it is becoming more and more widespread. One of such materials is Nitinol wich is an alloy composed by Ni and Ti. Nitinol was used to realise a coupling and decoupling device, due to its property to manifest itself in different ways when the temperature changes, under the action of an external force or by applying an electric current. The paper presents the main performances obtained after testing the thermocouple in the research laboratory regarding the coupling and decoupling of the two independent systems at different temperatures, the description of the utilised shape memory material, the determination of its braking torque and the advantages of using the thermocouple, especially rotary electrical machines of different sizes where their ventilation is required.

articleTitle: Design of EV Charging Station Controlled by PLC
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Today, the reducing of the gasoline consumption in the transport sector is realized by increasing the number of the number of electrical vehicles (EVs) and Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle - PHEV. But the number of charging stations must also be increased. In this paper the authors present a complete solution at an AC charging station in mode 3, according of International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61851-1 Standard, with PLC-HMI.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Panels Analysis Base On Simulink Tools
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this document a Simulink model for a photovoltaic array based on the components of Simulink library has been studied. The simulations performed in this document are based on the five-parameter model of a photovoltaic array. The equivalent scheme of a single diode is composed of a current source, a diode, a series resistance and a parallel resistance. The mathematical model of a photovoltaic panel (PV) was designed in MATLAB/Simulink environment, the I - V, and P - V graphics have been drawned. It was considered a real photovoltaic panel, namely the AFP 60-225, manufactured by Altius Solar. For representing the dependence between the level of solar irradiation, outside ambient temperature and the PV output values of the current, voltage and power is was used a PV cell existing in our laboratory.

articleTitle: Alternative Evaluation of Key Comparisons Results of the AC-DC Voltage Transfer Difference Standards
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Laboratories accredited by national accreditation bodies often use the calibration services of National Metrology Institutes. Those institutes are widely involved in key comparisons of its standards and have Calibration and Measurement Capabilities. These capabilities are published in the Key Comparison Database of the International Bureau of Measures and Weights based on key comparison results. Traditionally, key comparisons results are expressed in terms of the Degree of Equivalence of the National Metrology Institute standard with the its expanded uncertainty. In this case, no other characteristics are applied to evaluate of Calibration and Measurement Capabilities. This may make it difficult to select a calibration service for a specific National Metrology Institute by accredited laboratories. The paper presents the proposed alternative evaluation of key comparison results, which simplifies the analysis of National Metrology Institute calibration services in the presence of key comparison results with a number of comparison points. It provides for the use of the results obtained from key comparison of the E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> index as a criterion of data consistency. The practical application of the alternative evaluation for key comparison results for AC-DC voltage transfer difference is considered.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Type of Ring Permanent Magnets in Order to Achieve an Uniform Magnetic Field Around Them
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Permanent magnets are found in more and more devices in the industry and increasing their functional performance leads to the efficiency of these devices that contain them. The aim of this paper is the analysis by numerical modelling of different sets of ring permanent magnets to determine the optimal positioning of the magnetization directions in order to obtain an uniform magnetic field on their surface. The analysis of different sets of ring permanent magnets by numerical modelling, starting from simple structures formed by a ring magnet and progressively reaching complex structures formed by five magnets to determine the influence of magnetization direction on specific field quantities in order to find the optimal orientation of the magnetization direction to obtain an uniform magnetic field on the outer surface of the magnets. Two sets of ring magnets are analysed and compared. In the first set the same magnetization direction is considered in all magnets, and in the second set the magnetization direction will be different.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Surface Mounted PMSG for Stand-alone Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: There is a rapid growth in the use of permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) for wind energy conversion system (WECS) due to their high efficiency and power density. This paper emphasis on the analytical design and sensitivity analysis of a PMSG for a stand-alone direct drive WECS. In the initial part, an analytical calculation was performed in order to determine the design parameters for the surface mounted PMSG. In the second phase, the surface mounted PMSG was designed and analysed through finite element analysis (FEA). Mapping of electrical machine was done using the design specifications from the initial part. Sensitivity analysis was performed to check the machine behaviour at different electrical and mechanical loadings using three different topologies. Analysis of the surface mounted PMSG was done to achieve the maximum expected torque and voltage regulation in normal operation mode.

articleTitle: Influence of High Voltage Bundle Configurations on Human Exposure
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper is mainly dedicated to determining the influence of bundle conductors configurations on the electric and magnetic field levels determined at the standard height of 1 m above the ground. The technical-economic advantages are concisely presented, but also the inherent disadvantages of implementing such solutions. One of the main advantages is theoretically analyzed: the reduction of the risk of initiating corona discharges, as a result of the decrease of the potential gradient from the conductor surface, implicitly meaning the increase of the electric field strength near the ground. The theoretical approaches were reinforced by simulations performed with the help of ANSYS and EMFACDC software. It was considered the real case of a 400 kV network through which phase currents of 1050 A are transported, in three distinct variants: single conductor, double bundle and triple bundle. Electric field increases were found by 37% in the case of triple bundles, taking as reference a single conductor per phase. If the same total current is considered, the chosen bundle configurations have no influence on the generated magnetic field.

articleTitle: Integrated Learning in Electrical and Control Engineering Using an Educational Elevator System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The research of the authors is focused on presenting a practical multidisciplinary experiment - an elevator simulator to relate theory and practice inside of a lot of disciplines and to bring the “real world” into a useful case study for electrical and control engineering education. Through the existence of interesting experiments, students gain motivation either to continue thinking and improving new solutions for building and control of elevators. The concept of the modern elevator is presented in this paper from the perspective of integration of current technological equipment like a programmable logic controller, inverter, encoder, human-machine-interface on which students can develop various control strategies using a SCADA system. The paper presents the some exercises that students can perform on the existent simulator.

articleTitle: Optimizing Design of Transformers Used in Railway Traction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This research aims at reducing the exploitation costs for transformers used in electrical locomotives. The active and reactive electrical energy losses in these transformers are high, because they work with high electromagnetic stresses, imposed by certain gauge conditions. That is why, this paper reveals that this exploitation cost can be reduced by an optimal design of this transformer, taking also into account the restrictive conditions (gauge dimensions, short-circuit voltage. For example, in case of the transformer rated at 5500 kVA of the electrical locomotive, by an optimal design, the exploitation cost has been reduced with Ce= 14.53%= 67000 €, as against the existing transformer. The simulations carried out and presented justify the optimum constructive solution we have proposed.

articleTitle: High Frequency Analysis of the Vivaldi Antenna Parameters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to analyze the influence of different constructive elements of a Vivaldi antenna on its characteristic parameters (directivity, gain, S parameters). An initial antenna is considered and the substrate material, width of the microstrip line used as feeding and the shape of the planar metallic antenna are then modified. The antenna is modeled with a high frequency numerical modeling program, namely HFSS. The values of the parameters obtained for the different structures following different modifications will be compared with the ones of the initial antenna and an optimum antenna will be determined.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Electrical Energy Storage System for a Household with a Grid-Connected PV System using Inventory Model
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper focuses on sizing an energy storage system (ESS) for a household, which has a rooftop gridconnected photovoltaic (PV) system. The model developed is based on the single-period newsvendor model, which has been frequently used because both decision-making problems have the same objective, to determine the optimal capacity considering a stochastic supply and demand. The simulations were performed on different energy storage systems, taking into account the performance of both PV and ESS. Several parameters were integrated into the model in order to ensure an optimal sizing of the storage system. The results show that this approach minimizes the cost of the energy storage system and can be used to optimally size an ESS for a household, which has a rooftop grid-connected PV system.

articleTitle: Considerations about Rotor Current of an Asymmetrically Supplied Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: If an induction machine is powered by an asymmetric three-phase voltage system, asymmetric three-phase quantities of interest (voltages, currents, fluxes) result. The rotating magnetic field is no longer circular but elliptical. In addition the hodograph of all quantities have become elliptical. The dissymmetry factor of the rotor current depends on the dissymmetry factor of the supply voltage and also on the operating conditions. In practical applications there is a strong influence of both operating conditions and rotor speed on the asymmetric regime of the rotor quantities. The goal of this paper is to study to what extent the asymmetry of the rotor quantities depends on the operating conditions. This matter is studied by theoretical evaluation, confirmed and completed by simulation results.

articleTitle: Applying PrivateSky technologies regarding confidentiality in a wide spectrum of cloud based applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents an accounting application that is based on blockchain technology and uses the PrivateSky platform. The presented application can be easily adapted to any domain application (metrology, energy). It uses security and confidentiality principles applied by means of blockchain technologies and the authors present how these techniques can correct the main shortcomings of existing solutions on the market.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the measurement uncertainty in calibration of volumetric standard installation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)

authors.preferredName: Lecturer dr. eng. Gabriel Constantin Sârbu

abstract: The paper refers to evaluation of the measurement uncertainty in calibration of volumetric standard installation used for metrological verification of cold water meters. Is important to be interested in evaluation uncertainty of measurement simply because is necessary to make good quality measurements and to understanding and using the results. There is a particular reason for evaluation of measurement uncertainty, as part of calibration, where the uncertainty of measurement must be reported on the certificate. For evaluation the uncertainty of measurement, firstly we must identify the sources of uncertainty in the measurement, then we must estimate the contribution of the uncertainty from each source, finally the individual uncertainties are combined. The calibration of the installations used for the verification of the water meters is performed by the direct comparison method using secondary volume standards.

articleTitle: System for Study Stepper Motor Control and Clock Application
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper is presented a system which offers possibility to select some different method of command for a stepper motor. Specifically is presented possibility of command for a bipolar stepper motor. Development system offers possibility to drive a tower clock secondary.

articleTitle: Setting up a Distributed Control System Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a practical laboratory for student education purpose in Distributed Control Systems, with focus on applications for high voltage transmission substations. The monitoring, control and protection part is realized with a software platform and IED devices manufactured by AREVA T&D France, while the primary equipment, like circuit breakers and disconnectors are simulated with latched relays. The system architecture and communication network are reproducing a real one usually used in transmission substations. The implementation of this laboratory, both through specific laboratory works and experiments, makes the theoretical part to be supported by a practical experience, resulting in future graduates with added value in the electric power industry.

articleTitle: Influence of Soil Resistivity on 110 kV Substation Grounding System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the paper is presented a study related to the influence of soil resistivity on grounding system design for a 110 kV substation. The variation of the dispersion resistances and of the touch voltage and step voltage are studied depending on the soil resistivity. At the same time, the relationship between soil resistivity, touch voltages and site isolation are studied.

articleTitle: Alternative Evaluation of the Results of Key Comparisons of Electrical Capacitance Standards
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The practical application of traditional evaluation of the results of key comparisons of measurement standards may be difficult for accredited laboratories that wish to use National Metrology Institutes calibration service. Traditional using only the degree of equivalence of a National Metrology Institute standard with corresponding expanded uncertainty without any other characteristics for evaluating of calibration or measurement capabilities. The paper presents a proposed alternative evaluation of the results of key comparisons, which simplifies the analysis of National Metrology Institute calibration services. It envisages the use as a criterion of consistency of the obtained results of key comparisons of the E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> index to analyze of the degree of equivalence of National Metrology Institute standard and its expanded uncertainty. The practical application of the alternative evaluation for key comparison results for electrical capacitance standards is considered. This contributes to a more streamlined calibration of working standards of accredited laboratories for specific purposes.

articleTitle: Self-Consumption Indices Evaluation for a Residential Load Profile
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: With the increase interest in the use of energy from renewable sources, the trend of using photovoltaic sources has become higher, due to the advantages that this technology offers. Their use on a larger scale in the residential sector is increasingly encouraged, with more and more people trying to reduce the level of global pollution by using them. For grid connected systems, the most important indices referred to is that of self-consumption. This indicates the level of energy exchange between the network and the photovoltaic system, the lower this index means that the efficiency of energy use produced in photovoltaic mode is high. This paper presents an analysis of the self-consumption indices of a residential profile.

articleTitle: Electric Field in the Vicinity of High Voltage Deviation Towers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: There is a general concern about the impact that high voltage overhead power lines have on the environment, from the most diverse perspectives and points of view. One of the essential items to be addressed and resolved properly is the associated electric and magnetic fields, measured by convention, at a height of 1 m from the ground. Regarding strictly the generated electric fields, in the vast majority of cases, the registered values are below the limit of 5 kV/m, considered acceptable by the standards and norms in force. In this paper we have focused on the simulation of electric fields generated near a deviation tower, inside the angle having the tower itself as tip and the two alignments as sides. We have developed for our purpose a programming within the CST studio, a very powerful software much more used in the simulation of the radio frequency electromagnetic phenomena than of the extremely low frequency ones (the case of mains frequency). As a criterion for comparing the electric field emissions around a deviation tower, respectively a suspension tower, we used the current density induced along the vertical axis of a 3D human model previously proposed by the authors, also developed in CST Studio. Increases in the induced current density have been found, due to the summative-cumulative effects imposed by the angular configuration, both sides of the angle contributing to the induced current. Relative increases of over 50% have been found. However, these increases are offset by the height of the conductors. In the vicinity of the pylon the height is higher than in the middle of the distance between two consecutive towers, where the sag can reach values of 12 m. Another cause that contributes to attenuating the cumulative effects generated by the angled structure is the relative position of insulating chains. At deviation towers, they have an oblique position, raising the conductors higher from the ground than in the case of the suspension towers, where the position of the insulators is vertical. The simulated results show that human exposure in the area to electric fields near deviation towers is 30-40% higher than exposure in the area of a suspension tower but is perfectly comparable to human exposure in the middle of the distance between two consecutive towers, where sag reaches its maximum.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Determination in Waveguide Resonators with Lossy Dielectric Intrusions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper studies the influence of lossy dielectric intrusions in a cylindrical microwave resonator over the quality factor and resonance frequency. A comparison with analytical results for cavities with homogeneous filling is also performed.

articleTitle: Temperature Monitoring of the Heating Resistors of the Railway Switches from Romanian Railway System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper the temperature monitoring of the railway switches from Romanian railway system is presented. The system contains heating resistor, 6 k type thermocouple, SIEMENS PLC S7-1200 for processing information from thermocouple and autotransformer ATR8 for varying voltage and finally varying current trough heating resistor. The values of the parameters of the heating resistor system will be stored in PLC memory.

articleTitle: Study of Rechargeable Batteries Using a Laboratory Teaching Platform
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The aim of this work is a didactic one, namely to achieve simulation of a battery charge and discharge, the purpose being an educational one. The work deals with the design of a laboratory platform, a platform which was made for teaching purposes. By designing and implementing this application students will be able to put into practice the acquired theoretical knowledge. The practical realization is available to the students as a laboratory work for electrical measurements.

articleTitle: Model based design of an Urban Electric Minibus
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The public transport authorities in the cities have a great interest regarding the use of the means of transport with the lowest possible gas emissions. Electrification of the transport sector is one solution. Electric vehicles virtual developments occurs with the extend of the mobility technology and the needs for testing different configurations and energy management strategies. Using the model-based design method, an urban electric minibus model with advanced functional characteristics is defined. The software package Simcenter Amesim is used in the simulation processes based on the Model in the Loop philosophy. After describing all subsystem and their physics, their interaction will be highlighted at first and then analyzed to reach first conclusions in term of energy balance within the urban electric minibus.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition for Romanian Language using Deep Learning with DL-CNN convolutional layers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, we used the SRoL (Voiced Sounds of the Romanian Language) emotional corpus for Romanian language. We used a Deep Learning Neural Network (DL-CNN) to automatically recognition four emotions: joy, sadness, fury and neutral tone. A 3-layer deep learning neural network is used (two autoencoders are associated to the first two hidden layers and the third layer is a softmax layer). The best results of the emotion recognition obtained is 84,48% with fine tunning and 74.95% without fine tunning. It was noted that the percentages of emotion recognition provided by the MFSC - mel-frequency spectral coefficients are better than those obtained by the MFCC - mel frequency cepstral coefficients.

articleTitle: Methods and Techniques for Photovoltaic Solar Power Plant Monitoring and Wearing State Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents methods and techniques for monitoring the status and diagnosis of wear for each element in the architecture and operation of photovoltaic solar power plant. A typical configuration of photovoltaic solar power plant is: photovoltaic panel, junction box, connection cables, controller, battery and inverter. The first part of this study describes the methods and techniques often used in monitoring and diagnosing the state of a system. In the second part of the study is presented a new method and technique used in monitoring and diagnosing the state of a system, SMART FMECA. This new method will help to approach a better hierarchy of each failure mode, for each component.

articleTitle: Dielectric Spectroscopy Analysis of Composites Obtained from Thermoplastic with Feathers Flour
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article highlights the influence of poultry feather flour percentage and compatibilizers on the dielectric properties of composite materials based on low density polyethylene matrix. The behavior of composite materials was determined in terms of dielectric properties and the distribution of poultry feather flour in the basic polymer matrix, to optimize the technology and structure. The results showed that the addition of feather flour in thermoplastic matrix led to an increase in dielectric constant and dielectric loss and the presence of additives leads to better dispersion and processability of the composite material, an observation supported by X-ray analysis.

articleTitle: Gathering of Motion Data from an Arm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to collect the data of an upper limb through four sensors located on it. This data will be transmitted to a computer/laptop and will be processed later. The data obtained will be used in the future to control a robotic arm remotely in real time. This prototype can be used in various industrial fields, for example, the automotive industry, the assembly industry, the chemical industry, the defense industry. In order to highlight the movement of arm, the sensitive element used is of the resistive band type, which has the advantage of a low cost. This sensor is a variable resistor whose value decreases/increases when it is bent. The data are processed by an amplification circuit and are collected through an Arduino board that also communicates with a computer system for future processing. The obtained results highlight the viability of the adopted solution and open perspectives for development and improvement of equipment developed.

articleTitle: PLC Integration in the Grid Connection of a Non-Dispatchable Renewable Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The latest renewable energy sources are increasingly developing within today's society, with the main goal of reducing the global warming; but the rapidly development of these “green” power sources are having a high impact on the existent network connection, being unprepared for the high wave of connection requests to these types of sources. This situation leading often to delays in grid connection, various limitations imposed by authorities and in the end to abandoned projects. The grid owners have mandatory connection conditions to access the renewable source to their grid and one of the most actual solutions to comply with the imposed conditions is to integrate the PLC in the private connection station of the renewable source. The automatization of the connection stations should consider every part involved right from the first steps of the project. The purpose of this article is to identify and analyse the integration of a PLC in a non-dispatchable connection station. A flexible and organised component system was proposed as a solution which would allow a continuous and customisable PLC architecture. The strategy to have the PLC on the central position allowed a fluid information exchange between all the other equipment of the connection station. This setup allows the remote access and diagnose from the operation centre, being an advantage for an efficient maintenance, supervising and control. The information exchange between station components and the PLC has been validated by simulation using the PLC SIM program.

articleTitle: Measuring Luminance with Digital Photometric Camera in Short Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper refers to the measurement of luminance in a short straight tunnel using a digital camera that functions as luminance meter, as well as LMK mobile air device. The measurement of luminance had been conducted in the evening of January 2020 ans September 2020, in accordance of the standard EN 13201-4:2015 - Road lighting - Part 4: Methods of measuring lighting performance respectively. To consider the guide for the lighting of road tunnels and underpasses CIE 88:2004, from the analysis of the obtained results it is observed that the luminance is not adequate, i.e. they have values lower than the recommended minimum. In order to obtain a suitable lighting in accordance with the standard and the guide, it is necessary to redesign the lighting in the tunnel using LED luminaires with luminous and energetic efficiency superior to the HPS luminaires which currently illuminates the tunnel.

articleTitle: PCA-Based Analysis of Thermographic Data For the Estimation of the Parameters of the Electrical Motors’ Thermal Models
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The thermal models of the electrical machines are analytical representations that produce estimates of the thermal processes within their body. Nowadays, the implementation of non-contact apparatus such as infrared thermal cameras and image processing techniques allow in depth analysis of the thermal processes within the entire structure of the electrical machines. In this research, a 3D linear approximation model of the temperature distribution on the cross section of the machines and a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of the temperature distributions were implemented to obtain the parameters of an accurate model of the heating in the body of an asynchronous motor. The results of this research proved that, for the long term over torque operation or the full load coarse startup of the motor the model proposed in this work should be used to obtain better estimates. In this perspective, the classical model is a special case of the model proposed.

articleTitle: Distance measurements using 40L16 ultrasonic sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Distance measurements using time-of-flight (TOF) is a very important technique used in a wide variety of fields. One of the most used devices in ultrasonic ranging measurement is the HC-SR04 module. This module uses a threshold method for estimating distance. This paper presents a method based on cross-correlation, which improve the performance of the module's sensors. The two sensors, model 40L16 are 40LT16, respectively 40LR16, positioned face to face, of which 40LT16 is fixed, and 40LR16 positioned on a mobile target. Cross correlation is considered the optimal TOF estimation technique.

articleTitle: A New Solution of Electronic Device Proposed for Cereals, Vegetables and Fruits Storage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, some aspects related to store in good conditions the cereal products, vegetables, fruits, etc. are outlined, taking into account the storage time-period, easy to transport and saving fuel and time. The paper presents a prototype of a mobile container to be used for transport and storage in optimal conditions of cereals, vegetables and even fruits.

articleTitle: The Analysis, Modelling and Comparison between Circular and Rectangular Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Patch antennas are a type of antenna used in a lot of domains in our days, from GPS, radars and mobile phones to cancer tissue detection, spaceships, satellites and missiles. Their geometrical parameters and feeding type influence their functionality and characteristic parameters. This paper focuses on high frequency numerical modeling of circular and rectangular patch antennas with two different types of feeding. Four different types of antennas are high frequency analyzed to find their characteristic parameters. A comparation of the results obtained for the parameters of circular and rectangular patch antennas for different feeding types is detailed in order to find their influences on the frequency range in which the antenna is working.

articleTitle: Control System in Battery-Charging Regime for Autonomous Locomotives
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper is focused on a two stages control system for charging the battery of an autonomous locomotive. The existing traction inverter which operates as boost rectifier and a specific control strategy ensure unity power factor at the point of connection to the power supply. In the first stage, until an imposed value of the state of the charge is reached, a constant DC charging current is ensured. In the second stage, the charging at DC constant voltage finalizes the charging process of the battery. The synthesis of the parallel control system provides the parameters of both controllers involved (the voltage and current controllers). The proper design of the control system is validated by the simulation results. In addition, the good performance of the system (unity power factor, low harmonic distortion factor and high efficiency) is proved.

articleTitle: Lighting Optimization in a Short and Straight Tunnel, by Designing with Specialized Software
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This research paper refers to the optimization of lighting system on a straight and short tunnel, with a length of approximately 100 m and located in the Municipality of Resita in Romania, where the lighting is currently provided by luminaires equipped with HPS lamps. As the results of the light measurements, they do not correspond to the recommendations of the norms and standards in force, one redesigned the tunnel lighting system using authorized and specialized software SifisaLux-Tunel, because the tunnel lighting feature according to the standard is not currently available in DIALux evo nor in DIALux 4.13. By design, we used luminaires with LED modules with superior light and energy efficiency compared with existing HPS lamps. Through the results one obtained an optimized designing for the lighting system in the tunnel, in order to ensure a safety road traffic.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a Novel Latent Thermal Fluid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Phase Change Material Emulsions (PCMEs) were introduced by the latest researches as novel latent thermal fluids suitable for comfort cooling applications, solar thermal utilization, electronic systems etc. In order to be able to put these fluids into practice, particularly paraffin emulsion, many studies should be carried out as to present the major benefits it can bring in terms of energy efficiency, economy, sustainable development, environmental impact. These are recent proposed solutions, so studies in thermodynamic characteristics, thermal and rheological performance are therefore imperative in order to establish the benefits of their use in practical applications. The scope of this paper is to present experimental results for the thermodynamical properties of different versions of paraffin emulsions in order to be use as latent thermal fluid.

articleTitle: Application of Electricity Management Strategies for Lower Balancing Costs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Electricity is a commodity traded from the market through various products, but this level of accessibility represents a great opportunity and challenge for energy suppliers. Storing electricity in large quantities is not yet possible, meaning that the delivery to the customers needs to happen at the time of production. Energy suppliers must have a reliable strategy to buy or sell on the power market. The strategy efficiency determines if the supplier can optimally balance the portfolio, with the lowest impact on the overall costs. Energy imbalance is the difference between energy forecast and real consumption/ generation per portfolio. The cost of imbalances can negatively impact the margin of a portfolio that aggregates production, consumption, and trading. In this paper, the authors present complex situations for an energy supplier who needs to balance a portfolio consisting of consumption (industrial and commercial consumers), generation (photovoltaic and hydropower plants), and trading. The goal is to minimize market risk through excesses and shortfalls as much as possible and to reduce balancing energy expenses. Each market participant operating in the electricity market is obliged to have a contract with a BRP (Balancing responsible parties) or be one. The greater the number of participants in a group, the lower their balancing energy expenses, and keeping track of fluctuations both within a balanced group and with other balance groups can reduce costs.

articleTitle: Strategic and Mixed Learning Methodology in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Engineering education has been always a concern for universities and instructors. In this paper, a mixed learning approach model to teach at an engineering level via student involvement in a cross-curricular project is proposed. The methodology can be useful for an undergraduate course in digital signal processing. The proposed method involves the competencies acquired in other courses by the student and how to apply them to develop a project. Additionally, reinforcement methods to stimulate a deep approach to learning are presented. The assessment results imply that the proposed method enhances student motivation with the digital signal course and the engineering curriculum.

articleTitle: On the Cumulative Effect of Magnetic Fields in the Deviation Zones of Overhead High Voltage Power Lines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The magnetic fields emitted by Overhead Power Lines could be a reason for concern from the perspective of circular currents induced in the large surface parts of the human body, primarily of the trunk, an area where most vital organs are located. Our paper is dedicated to the study of the cumulative effects that are registered inside the obtuse angle having as tip a derivation tower and as sides the two consecutive alignments where the change of direction of the power line is made. The first part of the paper briefly reviews the already acquired background for measuring the magnetic field strength at the standard height of 1 m above the ground. The main elements of the simulation program made with the help of programming in CST Studio are presented. For the simulation, we used the concrete data provided by the project of the new 400 kV power line Gadalin-Suceava, Romania. To evaluate the cumulative effect, we compared the densities of circular currents induced in the trunk of a human rotational model, previously proposed and tested by the same group of authors. Conclusions have been drawn regarding the weight of the cumulative effects, which were reported both to the environment of a suspension tower of the same network and to a location at the middle of the distance between two consecutive towers. The conclusion is that at the level of 1 m above the ground the value considered as non-hazardous by the standards in force has not been exceeded. The cumulative effect introduced by the angular configuration of the power line does not exceed the increase due to lower clearance at the middle of the distance between 2 consecutive pylons.

articleTitle: Real Time Weather Location Traffic System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes the prototype of an automatic system for real-time determination and with a precise geographical location of the weather conditions in the environment of the car in which it is installed. The system we made, which we named it the Real Time Weather Location System, uses multiple sensors to retrieve weather data that it transmits to a central server and displays on a map accurate information about the weather conditions in different areas. Our system system is useful for alerting the authorities for natural disasters, such as: floods, storms, massive snowfalls, etc. Given the widespread use of motor vehicles, our system can be a viable alternative to current weather monitoring systems with a direct impact on the safety of car traffic participants as well as residents. At the same time, we designed and built the Real Time Weather Location System so that it is accessible to a wide range of car owners. The future development of our system aims at its compatibility with the means of railway and naval transport.

articleTitle: Identifying the Propulsion System Characteristics for a Battery Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents two simulation methods by which some characteristics of a propulsion system for an electric vehicle can be determined. Those characteristics refer to the torque, the power required at the wheels, the friction force, the air resistance force and others. Based on these characteristics a traction system that meets the requirements can be chosen. The study was performed on a prototype of an electric vehicle, Vector Model Zero. This paper highlights the results obtained using two software programs, namely Simcenter AMESIM and MatLAB Simulink, known throughout the academic world. The results provided by these software programs are compared at the end of this paper in order to verify their accuracy.

articleTitle: Supervision and Control System of an Electrical Equipment Testing Installation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: An electrical installation capable of providing both the permanent and short-circuit currents at which they are tested is required for testing electrical equipment. The paper presents a command and data acquisition system that allows the monitoring and control of some equipment within such a test installation. The paper presents experimental results of monitoring an electrical equipment inside the test installation, at which the current through the reinforcement motor was monitored, respectively, the currents through the closing and opening electromagnets, and these signals were analyzed to diagnose the technical condition.

articleTitle: Technical Condition Monitoring of Impedance Bonds using Sensors and Dedicated Device
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In nowadays, sensors technologies have expanded rapidly and have become cheaper. This has run to an increasing development in condition monitoring of systems, installations, structures, vehicles and also in railway transportation infrastructure using sensors and monitoring devices. This paper it proposes to present an experimental model of a monitoring device and its sensors for acquire data from an important electrical equipment of power supply system from electric traction, named impedance bond. The parameters which are acquired for that equipment are considered important and will lead to know its thermal stresses and real technical condition.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Particle Swarm optimization Applied on the Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch in Electrical Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The main purpose of the optimal reactive power dispatch (ORPD) is to reduce the active power losses by the right coordination of on-load tap-changing transformers (OLTC) and the reactive power resources, that may include capacitor banks and distributed generators. Additional to power losses, the voltage deviation minimization represents another aspect of interest in solving the optimal reactive power flow problem. Hence, the ORPD problem can be approached as a complex multi-objective optimization problem. Incorporating nonlinear functions, both continuous and discrete variables and numerous constraints, this problem requires highly performant computation methods for an efficient calculation of the optimal solution. In this regard, a multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) model is applied in this paper, in order to determine the ideal settings of distributed generators, transformers and capacitor banks for the proper operation of a distribution electrical system, in terms of active power losses and voltage profiles.

articleTitle: Simplified Mecanum Wheel Modelling using a Reduced Omni Wheel Model for Dynamic Simulation of an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Industrial and technical applications of omnidirectional mobile robots, with Mecanum wheels, are continuously gaining in importance because their excellent mobility, especially in areas with static or dynamic obstacles. The perspective of Industry 4.0 imposes an effective and efficient approach for production in general and then, specific to this application, to implement the control algorithm able to deliver to robot the deliberatively and reactively behaviour. An important tool to achieve these goals is virtualization of the prototype and his simulation in a 3D virtual environment.This paper presents a simplified method of modelling and kinematics simulation in Simscape Multibody™, taking an omnidirectional mobile robot with advantages related to simulation time. The necessary steps to develop inverse kinematics in robots and global reference frame, for specific omnidirectional mobile robot, are depicted in the paper using bottom-up approach with matrix transformation. The 3D modelling process starts from the CAD design, which is then transferred into a Simscape Multibody™ model in order to study the kinematic and dynamic characteristics. Four typical motion models including moving forward, moving laterally, moving in the diagonal direction and rotation have been simulated in Simscape Multibody™.

articleTitle: Mode Analysis In Planar Dielectric-Conductor Waveguides Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Determination of the critical wavenumbers, that appear when solving the Helmholtz partial differential equation for electric and magnetic field components in the case of dielectric waveguides, is treated in this paper as an optimization problem that has multiple solutions. The multimodal optimization problem (MMOP) is solved using genetic algorithms hybridized with a gradient based method. A study of the efficiency of power transmission for the different modes (solutions) is carried out using the analytical solutions for field components, with conclusions regarding the waveguide design for best performance.

articleTitle: Environmental pollution monitoring based on sensor network and open-software-open-hardware
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The quality of life in big cities is affected by different pollutants caused by human activities. To improve the environmental quality, continuous pollution monitoring is considered, which represents a crucial factor associated with the future decision regarding mobility in the city and activities localization. The paper presents a low-cost sensors network associated with pollution measurement in Lisbon. The monitoring system includes a set of sensors such as gas sensor, a temperature, humidity and pressure sensor, and a dust sensor. The localization of the environment measurement sites is carried out using a GPS module. The system prototype can be placed on buses or other vehicles for a distributed measurement in a specific region of the city. The autonomy of the system is assured through the usage of photovoltaic panels, which provide clean energy. The user accesses the information from the sensors through a web application. It also enables the consultation of a HeatMap with red, yellow, and green zones according to pollution levels. Related to the mobility and pollution level in the city, the application includes a specific functionality that allows creating a route with a starting point and endpoint specified by the user to avoid high polluted regions between two locations of the city. Experimental tests were performed regarding system autonomy, and a set of measurements was carried out mounting the system on an electric bike that traveled around the city of Lisbon.

articleTitle: GDPR Compliant Recruitment Platform using Smart Contracts and Executable Choreographies
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a recruiting application that is based on blockchain technology and uses PrivateSky platform, all ecosystem being developed in accordance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The presented application can be easily adapted to any industry recruitment methodology. It uses new privacy principles applied with help of blockchain technologies and the authors will present in the final paper some functionalities obtained with help of Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques.

articleTitle: Sustained Attention Detection System in Learning Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents a heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring system for the detection of attention status during learning activity. Developing an embedded system, the ECG and PPG signals are acquired simultaneously. Acquired signal primary including peak detection was applied to extract information about peak to peak time intervals that is used to calculate the HR abut also HRV. The primary processing data are sent in real time to a database in the cloud. Subsequently, HRV is analysed based on Matlab implemented algorithms considering time and frequency domains as so as non-linear measures. Several tests were carried out and the recorded results were analysed as the starting point to classify situations that capture the state of attention.

articleTitle: Study Upon the Influence of Bundle Configurations on Corona Losses
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the first part of our paper is presented in some details the issue of corona discharges produced in the immediate vicinity of the overhead high voltage power lines. The deterministic connection between the potential gradient at the surface of the active conductors and the initiation of corona discharges is theoretically approached. The decrease of electric field strength in the very surrounding area of the active conductors reduces the risk of corona discharges, but at the cost of increasing the electric field strength at the standard height (from the perspective of human exposure) of 1 m from the ground. We have considered a perfectly balanced 400 kV double-circuit three-phase overhead line, using suspension towers SN 400231, transmitting 1580 A (rms value) per phase in 4 distinct variants: a single conductor, respectively bundles of 2, 3 or 4 (parallel) subconductors. For each bundle, we have considered two representative types of spacer-dampers:side of 3 and 5 dm, respectively. For each case and sub-case, simulations have been performed using ANSYS and EMFACDC software, drawing the lateral profile of the electric field strength at three representative heights: 1 m from the ground, the height of the conductors (9 m) and the symmetrical height (above the conductors, 17 m from the soil). Useful conclusions have been drawn, both to reduce the risk of initiating corona discharges and to protect residential areas from electric field strength generated by the bundle-type configurations of over 220 kV overhead power lines.

articleTitle: The Influence of Parameters of a Power Transformer Winding Equivalent Distributed Circuit Model on Atmospheric Overvoltage Wave Internal Propagation along the Windings
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a study based on numerical simulation methods of electrical circuits - SPICE (Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis) family, which analyzes the influence of the variation of the parameters of the winding equivalent distributed circuit model of an electrical transformer on the propagation of overvoltage waves along the high voltage winding of the transformer. It is shown that of the five parameters of the equivalent circuit, the most important is the transverse capacitance, followed by longitudinal capacitance, winding resistance, winding inductance and with the least importance the transverse winding resistance of the transformer.

articleTitle: Adverse Light Environment: A New Challenge
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with light seen as a factor affecting human life comfort and health. The relative new concept defined as blue light related to artificial light was rapidly included in usual devices like phones, tablets, laptops and computer monitors or TV-sets as a selectable hardware option. A more important aspect is that of light fluctuations of the above mentioned screens due to what we are watching daily: movies, video games, commercials. Correlated with their high performance in technology, luminance, contrast, colours, resolution and dimensions, assimilating these screens with light sources is realistic. The light fluctuations or flicker or stroboscopic phenomenon can affect humans especially those with neural diseases but also normal people, mostly teenagers so dependent of modern gadgets. The paper is focusing on this last aspect presenting some research results following systematic measurements and records.

articleTitle: Informed Student – Guaranteed Success
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a case study resulting from the implementation of the project “Informed student-guaranteed success”, a project that aimed to familiarize young people with various aspects of the labour market. Within the project, the students involved carried out several documentation visits to various companies in the area and the region, and finally completed a questionnaire. Following the processing of the results, we identified the desire of young people for professional and personal development, as well as the interest and usefulness of study visits. The study allows the identification of intervention directions by educational institutions, employers, organizations and even the government. Thus, the use of modern teaching methods, combined with new technologies and visits to enterprises will contribute to the enhancement of the educational act and, implicitly, to the reduction of school dropout. In order to train the next generation, it is imperative to establish a close connection between economic agents and educational institutions, so that future graduates will be able to choose the right job, and adapt to the new status more quickly and easily. These documentation visits should be included in the activities of pre-academic students so that they can choose the right career.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Automatic Line Reclosure using PLC and Petri Nets Modelling
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of the line recloser automation sequence using PLC (Programable Logic Controller). The modelling of the automation process is done using the ordinary Petri Nets. There are presented several models corresponding to different line reclosure schemes. Then the implementation of the simpliest model model is done using Grafcet Language (the PLC programming language which becomes one of the most used language in the discreteand sequencial automation). An equivalance between PN modelling and Grafcet language is presented also here. This implementation represents an alternative to the classical hardwired reclosure automation scheme, (used even today in medium voltage networks), PC based softwares that runs on the servers in high voltage substations or dedicated (but rigid) functions existing in the expensive numerical protection relays.

articleTitle: LEDs and Measurements – How Much Light Source Influence the Measurement Results
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: When measuring the lighting conditions in an indoor or outdoor environment (e.g. illuminance or luminance) one should always consider the conditions at which the photometer was calibrated and the used light source. In spite of ban of incandescent lamps years ago, photometers are still calibrated with the CIE standard illuminants A, which is realized by incandescent lamp at color temperature of 2865 K. But the measured light sources are usually not incandescent or tungsten halogen lamp. In most cases indoor lighting uses fluorescent lamps and outdoor lighting HID lamps. Beside that more and more LED lamps are used both indoor and outdoor. For cases where photometer is calibrated with different light source as the measured one the ISO/CIE 19476:2014 standard “Characterization of the Performance of Illuminance Meters and Luminance Meters” [1] recommends use of spectral mismatch correction factors for correction of results. Although useful, spectral mismatch correction factors are difficult to calculate and apply. Especially if one does not know the spectrum of measured light source and the spectral responsivity of the used instrument. Measurements without application of spectral mismatch correction factors may, on the other hand, result in larger measurement error. The paper deals so with a question: how large the measurement error, when measuring the illuminance under different light sources, could be with a lux meter of class C and without the mismatch correction factor correction.
